questions.question_text: A very thin lining separates blood from surrounding tissue and permits rapid diffusion. Which epithelial arrangement best suits this role in capillary walls?
questions.explanation: Capillary endothelium is simple squamous epithelium: a thin single layer that supports exchange by diffusion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A nephron segment performs extensive reabsorption and secretion and is lined by cells with a cube-like profile and numerous mitochondria. Which epithelium is most likely?
questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal epithelium commonly lines kidney tubules; its cells can support active transport and secretion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A surface exposed to repeated friction needs several cell layers so superficial cells can be shed while deeper cells remain. Which tissue is best suited?
questions.explanation: Stratified squamous epithelium protects against abrasion; cells at the surface can be lost while basal cells replace them.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: As the urinary bladder fills, its lining changes shape while maintaining a protective barrier. Which specialised epithelium accommodates this stretching?
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium can stretch and alter cell shape as the bladder fills and empties.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A biopsy from a heart shows branching, striated muscle cells joined by intercalated discs. Which tissue is present?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is striated and branched, and its cells connect through intercalated discs for coordinated contraction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A muscle sample from the wall of an artery contracts without conscious control and lacks visible striations. Which muscle type is it?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle is non-striated and involuntary and occurs in walls of hollow organs and blood vessels.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A muscle fibre is long, striated and multinucleated, and its contraction is under voluntary control. Which tissue is it?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibres are typically striated, multinucleated and under voluntary control.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A tissue stores triglycerides, cushions organs and reduces heat loss. Which connective tissue is specialised for these functions?
questions.explanation: Adipocytes store fat; adipose tissue also cushions organs and provides thermal insulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A loose connective tissue fills spaces between organs and helps bind skin to underlying structures. Which tissue best fits?
questions.explanation: Areolar connective tissue is widely distributed beneath epithelia and around organs, where it binds and supports tissues.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Blood is classified as connective tissue even though its matrix is fluid. What is this matrix called?
questions.explanation: The extracellular matrix of blood is plasma, which carries cells and dissolved substances.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An airway lining appears multilayered because nuclei lie at different heights, yet every cell contacts the basement membrane. Which epithelium is this?
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium looks layered because nuclei are at different levels, although all cells contact the basement membrane.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a plant vascular bundle, most water-conducting vessel elements are dead at maturity, but one xylem component remains living. Which is it?
questions.explanation: Xylem parenchyma is living and can store materials; vessel elements, tracheids and fibres are generally dead at maturity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A stem thickens over successive years as a ring of dividing cells adds secondary xylem and phloem. Which meristem is responsible?
questions.explanation: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem that produces secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A bark layer limits water loss and blocks entry of many pathogens. Which substance in cork cells is chiefly responsible for its waterproofing?
questions.explanation: Cork cells have suberised walls; suberin makes the layer relatively impermeable to water and gases.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A waterlogged plant root contains large air spaces that aid internal gas movement and buoyancy. Which tissue modification is present?
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma is parenchyma with extensive air spaces, common in aquatic or waterlogged plants.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A phloem sieve-tube element loses its nucleus at maturity but remains functional through close association with another living cell. Which cell supports it metabolically?
questions.explanation: Companion cells maintain sieve-tube elements and support loading and unloading of sugars.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A seed coat is hard and resistant to compression because its supporting cells are thick-walled and lignified. Which plant tissue is chiefly responsible?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma has thick, lignified secondary walls and provides mechanical strength; mature fibres and sclereids are usually dead.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A transplanted skin graft fails to adhere because the basement membrane is damaged. What is one normal role of this thin extracellular layer?
questions.option_c: Anchoring epithelium to underlying connective tissue
questions.explanation: The basement membrane supports and anchors epithelium and helps separate it from underlying connective tissue.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A cartilage sample shows cells sitting in small spaces within a firm extracellular matrix. What are these cartilage cells called?
questions.explanation: Mature cartilage cells are chondrocytes and are housed in spaces called lacunae within the matrix.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Water moving through a root encounters a suberised barrier that blocks the apoplastic route into the stele. Which tissue layer contains this barrier?
questions.explanation: The Casparian strip in endodermal cell walls blocks apoplastic flow and forces water and solutes to cross a membrane before entering the vascular cylinder.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A ciliated lining in the oviduct moves the ovum toward the uterus. Which tissue feature directly produces this directional movement?
questions.explanation: Cilia on epithelial cells beat in a coordinated direction and help move material along the surface.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A dermal biopsy shows collagen bundles arranged in many directions, allowing resistance to stresses from different angles. Which connective tissue is present?
questions.explanation: Dense irregular connective tissue has collagen bundles arranged in multiple directions; it is found in the dermis and resists multidirectional stress.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient’s cartilage has poor repair capacity compared with a well-vascularised tissue. Which feature helps explain this limitation?
questions.option_a: Cartilage is made entirely of keratin
questions.option_b: Cartilage contains no living cells at any stage
questions.option_c: Cartilage has a direct artery inside every lacuna
questions.option_d: Cartilage is avascular, so nutrients diffuse through its matrix
questions.explanation: Cartilage lacks blood vessels; chondrocytes receive nutrients by diffusion through the matrix, contributing to slow repair.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A young stem bends in wind without snapping because its support tissue has living cells with unevenly thickened walls. Which tissue provides this flexible support?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides flexible support in growing plant regions; its living cells commonly have unevenly thickened primary walls.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
